subject: Hosted API commit tiers / price-lock & MFN discussion (BrightPath)
body:
Message 1/6
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Subject: Follow-up: usage tiers and rate protections

Hi Alyssa —

Great talking earlier. To summarize our pricing model for the Hosted API and the items we discussed:

- Per-token usage pricing with volume discount buckets (monthly commit tiers).
- Ability to attach a committed spend (monthly or annual) to unlock deeper per-token discounts and reserved capacity guarantees.
- Optional price-lock window (12 months) for committed tiers; outside of committed term, published list prices apply.
- Standard commercial negotiation points: Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) clause scope and CPI-linked caps on annual price increases.

Attached is the current rate sheet (BrightPath_Rate_Sheet_v3.pdf) and an initial MPA draft with suggested redlines. Can you confirm the monthly commit range you're targeting so we can map exact discount steps?

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm expected monthly token consumption for Q3–Q4 (ballpark is fine).
2) We map that to committed tiers and show net blended per-token rate.
3) Legal review of MFN and CPI-cap language (I can loop in Laura).
4) If acceptable, we produce a DocuSign-ready MPA and reserved capacity SLA notes.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Message 2/6
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:34:00 -0700
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightpath.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@brightpath.ai>
Subject: Re: Follow-up: usage tiers and rate protections

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the summary. Helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- We expect ~1.2B tokens/month by the end of Q3 if pilot goes well; ~2.5B by Q4 if we expand to the recommendations pipeline.
- We are interested in a 12-month price-lock if the commit tier is at least $75k/month.
- Procurement will push back on any open-ended MFN that would force us to match an unrelated customer’s deal structure. We can accept MFN on public per-token price tiers (i.e., list price) but not on privately negotiated credits/one-off concessions.
- Regarding CPI cap: we would like a maximum annual price increase tied to US CPI + 1% with a hard cap of 5%/year.

Can you get legal to propose language on the MFN carve-out and CPI cap? Also, do you offer any rebate mechanics if actual usage materially exceeds commit (i.e., overage discounts)?

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Chen | Head of AI Platforms | BrightPath.ai
alyssa@brightpath.ai

Message 3/6
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 10:47:00 -0700
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Subject: FW: BrightPath pricing points (legal input requested)

Rishi — looping in Laura and Marcus.

Laura — BrightPath has specific asks on MFN scope and a CPI-linked cap. They also want price-lock for 12 months on a $75k/mo commit. They asked about rebate/overage mechanics.

Marcus — SalesOps: can you model blended per-token rates for the two consumption scenarios Alyssa gave (1.2B and 2.5B tokens/month) with both committed and uncommitted pricing? Include reserved capacity surcharge assumptions if we allocate GPUs.

Thanks,
Priya

Message 4/6
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: FW: BrightPath pricing points (legal input requested)

Team — preliminary numbers attached (BrightPath_Rate_Sheet_v3.pdf has the mapping). Quick summary:

- At 1.2B tokens/mo: uncommitted blended rate ~ $0.0009/token. With a $75k/month commit we can push blended to ~$0.00062/token (approx 31% savings).
- At 2.5B tokens/mo: uncommitted rate ~ $0.00085/token. With a $150k/month commit blended ~ $0.00045/token (approx 47% savings).
- Reserved capacity (dedicated pool) surcharge estimated at +12% to cover GPU reservations if they require burst guarantees.

I also sketched an overage ladder: once usage exceeds 120% of committed monthly tokens, incremental tokens billed at committed rate minus additional 10% rebate (so a softened overage hit). It’s conservative but keeps the economics friendly.

Marcus
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightPath_Rate_Sheet_v3.pdf

Message 5/6
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 08:09:00 -0700
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightpath.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@brightpath.ai>
Subject: RE: Hosted API commit tiers / price-lock & MFN discussion (BrightPath)

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below are redline suggestions and positions from legal:

1) MFN: We can agree to an MFN limited to published per-token list prices and non-discriminatory published tier discounts. We will explicitly exclude privately negotiated credits, promotional one-offs, and customer-specific integration credits. Suggested clause: "MFN applies only to published per-token list rates and defined published discount tiers, and excludes bespoke credits, promotional concessions, and implementation credits."

2) CPI cap / price increase: Redwood proposes annual price adjustments tied to US CPI, capped at 4% per year. We cannot accept a hard cap of 5% plus CPI; 4% cap is our standard for enterprise MPA.

3) Price-lock window: we can provide a 12-month price lock on list per-token rates for customers who commit to a minimum $75k/month for 12 months. If BrightPath wants price-lock on net/blended effective rate (post discounts), we need contract language stating that any mid-term material changes to consumption profile or reserved capacity requirements allow a rate rebalancing conversation.

4) Overage / rebates: acceptable to offer a graduated overage rebate ladder (Marcus’s proposal looks fine). We will include a clause for reconciliation at the end of each quarter to true-up committed vs actual usage and rebate/credit any eligible overage discounts.

I’ll attach a marked MPA (MPA_Draft_2026_redlines.docx) with the proposed language. If we need to concede to a 5% CPI cap we’d want a commercial concession (e.g., reduced reserved pool surcharge or an expanded support package).

Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MPA_Draft_2026_redlines.docx

Message 6/6
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightpath.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@brightpath.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tiers / price-lock & MFN discussion (BrightPath)

Laura / Rishi —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the redlines. A couple quick responses:

- MFN carve-out sounds reasonable. We’ll push Procurement to accept an MFN limited to published list tiers (that should be a win).
- CPI cap: BrightPath prefers 5% hard cap (they want protection vs runaway cloud costs). If Redwood can’t move from 4% to 5%, we’d consider the concession Laura noted (waive the reserved capacity surcharge for the first three months). Can you quantify that concession?
- Overage ladder / quarterly reconciliation: agreed in principle. We need the true-up language to ensure credits appear on the next invoice.

Procurement — I’ll circulate our internal redlines but expect the next step is a final MPA with the MFN carve-out language and the CPI cap callout (we can accept 4% if Redwood confirms the reserved capacity concession).

We’re targeting signature before end of April if terms are finalized.

Thanks,
Alyssa

[End of thread]
